nodes.text: water stands in pools, stiff with everlasting cold;
a muddy marsh surrounds the sluggish spring.
When the aged priest set foot in this place,
he did not delay: the place supplied the night.
Then the earth was dug out, and on it, snatched from pyres,
fires are thrown; the seer himself covers his body
in a funereal mantle, and shakes a bough;
a mourning robe flows down over his feet;
in squalid dress the grim old man advances;
death-bearing yew binds his white hair.
Sheep of black fleece and dark cattle
are dragged inside; the flame preys on the offerings,
and the living beasts quiver in the funeral fire.
Then he calls the shades, and you who rule the shades,
and him who keeps the barriers of the Lethaean lake;
he rolls over a magic chant, and, menacing, with raving
mouth sings out whatever either appeases the flitting
shades or compels them; he pours blood on the altars
and burns the beasts whole, and with much gore
soaks the cave; he pours as well the snowy
liquid of milk, and pours out wine with his left
hand, and chants again, and, gazing at the ground,
summons the shades with a deeper, frenzied voice.
Hecate's pack barked; three times the hollow valleys
rang mournfully; the whole earth, its ground shaken,
was struck. “I am heard,” says the seer,
“I have poured out words that take effect: blind chaos bursts open,
and a way to the upper world is given to the peoples of Dis.”
The whole wood sank down and raised its leafy hair,
the oaks split with cracks, and the whole grove
shook with dread; the earth drew back
and groaned deep within: whether hidden Acheron
took it ill that its depths were probed,
or the earth itself, to give the dead a way,
crashed as its frame burst; or, raging with anger,
three-headed Cerberus shook his heavy chains.
Suddenly the earth gapes, and, loosened in a vast
chasm, lay open. I myself saw the sluggish lakes
among the shades, I myself the pale gods
and true night; ice-cold in my veins the blood stood still
and stuck fast. A savage band sprang forth,
and the whole viper-born race stood in arms,
the troops of brothers sown from the Dircaean tooth.
Then grim Erinys shrieked, and blind Frenzy
and Horror, and all that the eternal darkness
breeds and hides: Grief tearing out her hair,
and Disease, barely holding up her weary head,
Old Age, a burden to herself, and hovering Fear,
and Plague, the greedy bane of the Ogygian people.
Our courage left us; she herself who knew the old man's rites
and arts was stunned; the father, undaunted
and made bold by his loss, summons the bloodless crowd
of fierce Dis. At once, like light mists,
they flit about and breathe the air of the open sky.
Eryx does not bring forth so many falling leaves,
nor does Hybla make so many flowers in mid-spring,
when the swarm is knit into a dense, tight ball,
nor does the Ionian sea break so many waves,
nor do so many birds, fleeing the threats of icy Strymon,
exchange winters and, cutting through the sky,
trade northern snows for the warm Nile,
as the peoples that the seer's voice drew forth.
Eagerly they seek the hiding places of the shady grove,
the trembling souls; first from the ground emerges,
